tldr: EvolveSearch is an iterative self-evolution framework combining reinforcement learning (RL) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to enhance LLM agentic web search capabilities without any human-annotated reasoning data, achieving a 4.7% average improvement over the current state-of-the-art across seven MHQA benchmarks.
contributions: Proposes EvolveSearch, the first framework to iteratively combine RL with SFT to enhance LLMs' web search capabilities
Eliminates the need for human-annotated reasoning data by leveraging high-quality RL rollouts for continuous self-improvement
Demonstrates significant effectiveness and generality across multiple MHQA datasets through extensive empirical evaluation
methods: The framework divides training data into N parts and iteratively alternates between two stages across 10 iterations. In Stage 1 (RL phase), the model performs reinforcement learning using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a hybrid reward combining format reward and answer reward, generating 16 rollouts per sample with a batch size of 128. In Stage 2 (SFT phase), rollouts are filtered using three rules—High-Reward Selection (δ=0.7), Same Query Deduplication, and Multi-Calls Selection (top k=2000)—then used for Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT) to produce a better cold-start model for the next RL iteration. Experiments use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the backbone with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as the judge model, trained on 80,000 samples from NQ, TQ, HotpotQA, and 2Wiki.
results: EvolveSearch achieves a 4.7% average improvement over the previous state-of-the-art across seven MHQA benchmarks. After 3 iterations, it reaches 76.2% average in-domain accuracy and 53.7% out-of-domain accuracy, consistently outperforming all baselines including DeepResearcher (73.2% ID, 50.3% OOD) and DeepResearcher* (73.2% ID, 50.3% OOD). It also shows strong generalization across out-of-domain datasets (Musique: 33.8%, Bamboogle: 77.1%, PopQA: 50.3%). The iterative RL-only baseline (RLSearch-ite3) achieved 73.8% ID and 53.2% OOD, demonstrating that SFT cold-start provides a meaningful advantage.
limitations: Requires a large judge model (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct) for reward computation, which may be computationally expensive
Performance with different judge models (e.g., DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o, Grok-3) was slightly lower than the trained judge model, though improvement trends remained consistent
The hybrid reward format constraint (requiring exact tag matching) may bias the model toward certain rollout patterns
Experiments were limited to 3 reported iterations despite using N=10 data partitions
